key_insight: A scalable causal Bayesian network framework (UPEBNL) makes large EHR-based cancer prescreening more interpretable by learning directed, evidence-propagation relationships instead of only black-box associations.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help clinicians and researchers inspect risk pathways and prioritize prescreening signals for esophageal and colorectal cancer from routine health records.
method: Adaptive data slicing to split large EHR data for parallel learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to combine stable network edges
Global DAG construction to produce an interpretable causal network
evidence_signal: In simulations, UPEBNL improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and was up to 221.28-fold faster; in EHR prescreening it achieved AUCs of 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: The learned causal directions are still based on observational EHR data, so confounding and site-specific data quality may affect generalizability and implementation.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
